lead: To show an app, the real screen is more convincing than any animation. video-demonstrativo drives a browser through your app, takes a photo at each step with the position of the clicked element, narrates with a local voice, and assembles the video with cursor and zoom. In this lesson you do all of it, with a sample app, at no credit cost.
objetivo: capture an app step by step with the agent and render the narrated demo that passes the checker.

aprende.t: The actions.json: URL, screen size, and one step per click
Capture with agent-browser: a screenshot and the target position for each step
Local narration per step, with the Kokoro voice, no external service
The generated composition and the render with the HyperFrames version pinned

hero_alt: Laptop on a dark desk showing an app with a circle highlighting the cursor, and a second monitor with the same screen enlarged.

secoes.titulo: From the live app to the MP4

nos.detalhe: URL, fixed viewport and the list of steps: what to do (fill, click, clickText, setValue, wait), which element to aim the cursor at, the on-screen caption and the narration line.
Drives agent-browser through the real app, takes a screenshot for each state (assets/shots/NN-id.png) and measures the target's box with getBoundingClientRect. Writes steps.json.
One line per step plus the closing, each in its own WAV, using HyperFrames' own Kokoro pf_dora voice. Nothing leaves your machine.
The composition-template.mjs measures each WAV and writes the index.html: browser window, a cursor that moves to the target, click, zoom and caption timed to the narration.
HyperFrames check and render, with the version pinned in the commands. Then the kit's checker verifies duration, size and audio.

secoes.legenda: Steps of the video-demonstrativo skill at commit a87b382 (Oct 5, 2026). Capture before animating: the video shows the real screen.

secoes.sub: The block serves the app on a local port, runs the capture in its own agent-browser session and shuts everything down at the end.

blocos.conteudo:
K=~/projetos/formacao-cinema-ia-fabrica-v72/kit
command -v agent-browser > /dev/null || { echo "FALTA agent-browser: npm i -g agent-browser@0.6.0 && agent-browser install"; exit 1; }
E=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-fabrica/a3; rm -rf "$E"; mkdir -p "$E"; cd "$E"
git clone -q https://github.com/inematds/video-demonstrativo.git && git -C video-demonstrativo checkout -q a87b382
cp video-demonstrativo/skills/video-demonstrativo/scripts/capture.mjs "$K/exemplos/a3-demo/actions.json" .
python3 -m http.server 18791 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory "$K/exemplos/a3-demo" > servidor.log 2>&1 & S=$!
until curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:18791/; do sleep 0.3; done
export AGENT_BROWSER_SESSION=ensaio-fabrica
node capture.mjs actions.json > captura.log 2>&1; echo "captura: $?"
agent-browser close > /dev/null 2>&1; kill $S
ls assets/shots
python3 -c "import json; s=json.load(open('steps.json')); print('passos no steps.json:', len(s['steps']))"

abas.html:
captura: 0
00-home.png
01-minutos.png
02-ritmo.png
03-calcular.png
04-resultado.png
passos no steps.json: 5

One screenshot per step and the steps.json with the measured boxes. The until curl waits for the port to respond before opening the browser; a fixed sleep fails on a loaded machine.

The block stops at the first line with FALTA agent-browser: npm i -g agent-browser@0.6.0 && agent-browser install. The package is Apache-2.0 (npm, Oct 19, 2026); the install downloads the browser. The session AGENT_BROWSER_SESSION=ensaio-fabrica avoids touching another session you may have open.

secoes.sub: Creates the HyperFrames project, copies screenshots, fonts and steps.json, generates one narration line per step and writes the composition.

blocos.conteudo:
export HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1 NO_COLOR=1
E=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-fabrica/a3; S=$E/video-demonstrativo/skills/video-demonstrativo
cd "$E" && rm -rf demo
npx -y hyperframes@0.8.176 init demo --non-interactive > init.log 2>&1; echo "init: $?"
cd demo && mkdir -p assets/audio assets/txt
cp -r ../assets/shots assets/ && cp -r "$S/assets/fonts" assets/ && cp ../steps.json .
cp "$S/scripts/composition-template.mjs" build-demo.mjs
node -e 'const d=require("./steps.json"); const l=d.steps.map(s=>s.narration); l.push(d.ctaNarration);
l.forEach((t,i)=>require("fs").writeFileSync(`assets/txt/s${i+1}.txt`, t.trim()+"\n")); console.log("falas:", l.length)'
for f in assets/txt/s*.txt; do
  n=$(basename "$f" .txt)
  npx -y hyperframes@0.8.176 tts "$f" --voice pf_dora --lang pt-br --speed 0.98 --output "assets/audio/$n.wav" > /dev/null 2>&1 || echo "falhou $n"
done
ls assets/audio | wc -l
node build-demo.mjs | head -1

abas.html:
init: 0
falas: 6
6
index.html gerado · 1920x1080 · TOTAL=30.389s · 6 cenas (5 passos + CTA)

Six narration lines (five steps and the closing), six WAVs. The TOTAL comes from the sum of the lines plus a gap before and after each one: change the line, and the duration changes.

The skill at commit a87b382 calls npx hyperframes without a version, and the old course pinned 0.8.66. The blocks in this course use hyperframes@0.8.176 (npm, Oct 19, 2026) and HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1. The why, and the rest of HyperFrames, is in course 3.

secoes.sub: Check, draft render and the checker, using the duration the composition itself declares.

blocos.conteudo:
export HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1 NO_COLOR=1
K=~/projetos/formacao-cinema-ia-fabrica-v72/kit
cd ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-fabrica/a3/demo
npx -y hyperframes@0.8.176 check 2>&1 | grep -E "◇|✗" | head -3
npx -y hyperframes@0.8.176 render --quality draft --workers 2 --quiet --output renders/demo.mp4 > render.log 2>&1
echo "render: $?"
D=$(grep -o 'id="root"[^>]*data-duration="[0-9.]*"' index.html | grep -o "[0-9.]*\"$" | tr -d \")
echo "duração pedida: $D s"
python3 "$K/conferir.py" renders/demo.mp4 "$D" 1920x1080 --audio; echo "saída: $?"

abas.html:
◇ 0 errors, 0 warnings

  ◇ 0 errors, 0 warnings
render: 0
duração pedida: 30.389 s
OK: 30,4 s · 1920×1080 · 30 fps · com áudio
saída: 0

On this machine the 30 s render took less than a minute (measured outside the capture; software render, --workers 2). The requested duration comes from the root's data-duration, so the checker works for any script of yours.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after you answer.

perguntas.p: Why is the viewport in actions.json fixed?
opcoes: So the render finishes faster on a busy machine.
Because the measured boxes and the photos have to match.
So the narration for each step fits in the time.
perguntas.explica: The cursor aims at the box measured with getBoundingClientRect. If the capture screen and the photo have different sizes, the click shows up outside the button.

perguntas.p: What sets the final length of the demo?
opcoes: The number of steps times 5 s, fixed.
The size in pixels of the capture photos.
The length of each spoken line, plus some slack before and after.
The value of --fps passed to the render.
perguntas.explica: build-demo measures each WAV and builds the scene around the speech. Longer speech, longer scene.

perguntas.p: The block waits for the app's port with an until curl loop. Why not sleep 1?
opcoes: The server may take longer than 1 s.
Because the sleep command doesn't exist on macOS or WSL.
Because curl speeds up the local Python server startup.
Because agent-browser requires curl to run before it.
perguntas.explica: Waiting for the state (the port responds) and not for the clock is what makes the block repeatable on any machine.

itens.texto: agent-browser photographs the real app and measures where to click.
each step lasts as long as its narration, made with a local voice.
HyperFrames 0.8.176 in the blocks, checker on the MP4.
